items.claim: The row's a-fortiori (qal wahomer) reading of 11:31 and its rejection of a cluster with 11:30 are byte-true and well warranted.
items.evidence: MT 11:31 opens with הֵ֣ן … אַ֝֗ף כִּֽי (oshb:Prov.11.31, byte tier), the standard qal-wahomer "behold ... how much more" construction, distinct from 11:30's tree-of-life image (oshb:Prov.11.30). The only token 11:31 shares with 11:30 is the ubiquitous tsaddiq (righteous), not a distinguishing catchword, so treating 11:31 as its own single_proverb in the C2 sentence collection default (book_strategy Prov.md section 6) is correct.

items.claim: The negation-particle antithesis in 12:3 is byte-true, but the row's rejected_alternative misdescribes which neighboring verse carries which content and in which direction.
items.evidence: 12:3's A-colon negates with the ordinary lo and its B-colon with the rarer poetic bal (oshb:Prov.12.3, byte tier), a real construction supporting the single_proverb call. But rejected_alternative calls the crown/rottenness imagery "the crown/rot verse before it" -- that imagery belongs to 12:4, the verse AFTER 12:3, not before it (oshb:Prov.12.4). It also names an unidentified "counsel verse after it", but no verse immediately following 12:3 carries counsel content; 12:2, the actual verse BEFORE 12:3, speaks of Yahweh's favor and a wicked man's mezimmot (plans/schemes), not counsel (oshb:Prov.12.2). The stated rival is not the verse the row claims it to be, at the position it claims -- before/after are swapped and the content is misattributed.

items.claim: The asyndeton claim for 12:5 is byte-true and the shared-vocabulary dismissal against 12:6-12:7 is defensible.
items.evidence: 12:5's B-colon (tachbulot resha'im mirmah) opens with no waw at all (oshb:Prov.12.5, byte tier), unlike every other verse in the immediate run 12:1-12:4 and 12:6-12:7, which all mark the B-colon with a coordinating waw (oshb:Prov.12.1-Prov.12.4, oshb:Prov.12.6-Prov.12.7). The disclosed catchword resha'im (wicked, plural) recurring across 12:5-12:6-12:7 is real (sweep.py --heb resha'im, skeleton tier: 40 book-wide occurrences spread across roughly 20 chapters), so it reads as ordinary collection-wide antithesis vocabulary rather than a construction unique to this three-verse run comparable to the 26:4-5 answer/answer-not pair; the single_proverb call stands.

items.claim: The construct-phrase-vs-header distinction for 12:6's opening divrei is correctly drawn against the device inventory.
items.evidence: Divrei resha'im at 12:6 is verse-initial (oshb:Prov.12.6, byte tier) but the device inventory's own headers table names only Prov.30.1 and Prov.31.1 as book/collection header verses, not 12:6 (prov_device_inventory.json collection_seams.headers, tier-1). The row's book-wide count of 19 for the word matches the toolkit-sanctioned skeleton-tier sweep (sweep.py --heb divrei, skeleton tier: 19), and the adversative waw opening the B-colon (u-fi yesharim) is verified.

items.claim: The two-predicate-vs-one-predicate colon asymmetry in 12:7 is byte-true and the dismissal of a 12:5-12:7 catchword cluster is internally consistent with the adjacent row.
items.evidence: 12:7's A-colon carries two predicates, hafokh and ve-einam, against the B-colon's single ya'amod (oshb:Prov.12.7, byte tier). The shared resha'im term with 12:5-12:6 is disclosed and dismissed on the same book-wide-vocabulary grounds verified for the 12:5 row (40 occurrences, sweep.py --heb resha'im, skeleton tier), so the two rows' calls are consistent with each other rather than contradictory.

items.claim: The snare-image/hearing-verb argument for 12:13 and its rejection of a 12:13-12:14 pairing are byte-true.
items.evidence: Moqesh (snare) frames the A-colon and the vav-consecutive va-yetse opens the righteous party's escape in the B-colon (oshb:Prov.12.13, byte tier). 12:14 uses the distinct noun peri (fruit, not pesha transgression) and its own waw (u-gmul) is non-adversative since 12:14 is synthetic rather than antithetic -- it has no "but" contrast (oshb:Prov.12.14; web:Prov.12.14 carries no adversative in WEB either). The row's claim that 12:14 "lacks an adversative waw altogether" is accurate under that reading.

items.claim: The hearing-verb-only-in-the-wise-colon argument for 12:15 is byte-true and the shared fool-noun dismissal against 12:16 is defensible.
items.evidence: 12:15's B-colon alone supplies a verb of hearing, ve-shomea (oshb:Prov.12.15, byte tier), against the A-colon's bare self-assessment. The disclosed catchword evil (fool) shared with 12:16 is real (sweep.py --heb evil, skeleton tier: 17 book-wide occurrences spread across roughly 10 chapters), but 12:15-12:16 is the sole adjacent pair among all of them, and the two verses argue unrelated points -- epistemic self-assessment versus emotional self-control -- rather than sharing a repeated construction on the model of the 26:4-5 answer/answer-not pair, so resisting a cluster call here is defensible.

items.claim: 12:16's own bicolon reading is byte-true, but its claim that no other antithetic pair in the chapter carries a temporal qualifier is byte-false.
items.evidence: 12:16 does open with the temporal ba-yom ("in that day"; oshb:Prov.12.16, byte tier) framing the fool's exposed vexation. But 12:19, three verses later in the same chapter, is also antithetic -- “but a lying tongue is only momentary” (web:Prov.12.19) -- and carries two temporal qualifiers of its own, la'ad ("forever") and ad-arginah ("for a moment") (oshb:Prov.12.19, byte tier). That is a direct counter-example to the row's unsourced universal claim that the chapter's other antithetic pairs lack a temporal qualifier: no digit-bearing sweep supports the claim, and the plain text falsifies it.
